Title: Diagnosis of test `testJira567`

Details:
The test `testJira567` checks the behavior of the method `ArrayUtils.addAll` when combining arrays of different but related types. Specifically, it tests these cases:
1. Adding a `Long[]` array to a `Number[]` array, which is valid since both are subtypes of `Number`.
2. Adding a `Long[]` array to an `Integer[]` array, which should throw an `IllegalArgumentException` because `Long` cannot be stored in an `Integer` array.

Examining the implementation of `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...)`:
- The method uses the component type of the first array (`array1`) to create a new array of the combined length.
- It copies `array1` elements followed by the elements from `array2` into the new array.
- The method does not explicitly check whether elements in `array2` are compatible with the component type of `array1`.
- It simply creates the result array by `Array.newInstance(type1, array1.length + array2.length)` where `type1` is the component type of `array1`.
- When copying `array2` elements into `joinedArray`, if any element of `array2` is not assignment compatible with `type1`, the runtime will throw an `ArrayStoreException` (not an `IllegalArgumentException`).

This explains the test failure:
- The test expects `IllegalArgumentException` when incompatible types are combined.
- Instead, the real failure is due to incompatible type assignment which causes a runtime `ArrayStoreException`.
- The code lacks a check to detect type incompatibility and to throw the expected `IllegalArgumentException`.

The faulty behavior arises because the method does not validate the compatibility of all elements in `array2` against the component type of `array1` before array creation and copying.

Suggested methods to fix:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...)`

This method should ideally include a check to ensure all elements of `array2` are assignment compatible with `array1`'s component type and throw an `IllegalArgumentException` if not.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
